mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 4% for a month, increased labor market participation and consumer confidence drive a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates sustained economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% for a month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positively correlated with UNRATE change (slope < 0.1, p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) relative to GDP for two consecutive months signals robust demand, prompting a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate future earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no significant correlation with GDPC1 growth (R-squared < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production for three months indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which typically precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates soft landing difficulties.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 237) combined with higher FEDFUNDS create a dual pressure that produces a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return by raising discount rates.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 237 and FEDFUNDS rises in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant negative effect of CPIAUCSL-FEDFUNDS interaction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate below 5% triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market expects wage growth to support equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher when UNRATE drops (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When personal income (not directly observable but proxy via HOUST) rises faster than consumer spending (GDPC1), it suggests pent-up demand and a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST growth exceeds GDPC1 growth for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns show no significant positive effect of the HOUST-GDPC1 interaction (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL trend down) and rising consumer confidence (not directly observable but assumed via context), S&P 500 forward returns tend to be positive over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: regime: CPIAUCSL trend down for 3 months
failure_condition: In the identified regime, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).
